newsitem.title: USA: Late Brent trade in the U.S. weakens paper prices.
newsitem.headline: Late Brent trade in the U.S. weakens paper prices.

text.p: North Sea Brent paper traded weaker in the U.S. aftermarket window, deflating prices from the IPE settlement on a slew of outright deals late Wednesday.
Foreign crude traders said there were a total of 11 outright May Brent partials moved, and an additional three inter-month spreads.
On an outright basis, 800 lots were moved at $20.22 in seven different EFP (exchange for phsyical) deals, declining 11 cents from the May IPE settle at $20.33 per barrel.
Cash May Brent moved for 500 lots in three separate deals at $20.24, and again for 100 lots at $20.20, traders said.
The three spreads saw U.S. refiners buy two April/May Brent spreads at plus 14 cts, and a May/July at plus 23 cts.
Spread deals were slightly weaker for all three trades from levels pegged ahead of the aftermarket window.
